crossRefs.note: When the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed to her a certain officer, saying, “Restore all that…
He said to him, “Say now to her, ‘Behold, you have cared for us with all this care. What is to be done for you? Would…
As the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried to him, saying, “Help, my lord, O king!”
When the woman of Tekoa spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, showed respect, and said, “Help, O king!”
“Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Maintain the rights of the poor and oppressed.
Rescue the weak and needy. Deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.”
He judged the cause of the poor and needy; so it was well, then. Wasn’t this to know me?” says Yahweh.
A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’

people.name: Philistia
people.line: An ancient people and region in Canaan

translations.web: At the end of seven years, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines. Then she went out to beg the king for her house and for her land.
translations.bsb: At the end of seven years, when the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, she went to the king to appeal for her house and her land.
translations.kjv: And it came to pass at the seven years' end, that the woman returned out of the land of the Philistines: and she went forth to cry unto the king for her house and for her land.
translations.asv: And it came to pass at the seven years' end, that the woman returned out of the land of the Philistines: and she went forth to cry unto the king for her house and for her land.
